subject.title: fix(qa): reject runtime tool intent without result evidence

question: Should QA Lab intentionally stop treating the eight Codex-native workspace rows as required runtime-tool coverage until native command/file-operation outcomes are represented as canonical evidence?
rationale: This is a release-validation policy boundary: the implementation is internally consistent, but maintainers must decide whether reduced asserted coverage is preferable to retaining false-positive required rows.

options.title: Accept the scoped evidence boundary
options.body: Merge the change so required coverage remains limited to result-backed OpenClaw dynamic tools and the unsupported native rows remain visible as secondary diagnostics.

options.title: Retain the old required rows
options.body: Keep the broader gate only if maintainers define a concrete native Codex outcome-evidence contract that can prove those rows rather than relying on intent or report text.

recommendation.title: Accept the scoped evidence boundary
recommendation.body: Merge the change so required coverage remains limited to result-backed OpenClaw dynamic tools and the unsupported native rows remain visible as secondary diagnostics.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged work owns the persisted runtime-evidence and runtime-pair execution boundaries that determine this QA contract.
